title: The Clockwork Swan Affair
summary: SirLocked and his companion investigate a rain-soaked exhibition at Halcyon House, where a prophetic automaton writes an accusation moments before its inventor vanishes from a locked workroom. The inquiry moves through guests, mechanisms, canal evidence, and Bellweather's watchmaker trade before the swan's message can be understood.

characters.name: Lady Maribel Quince
characters.description: Elegant, commanding, and visibly terrified that the evening's disaster will ruin both her reputation and her fortune.

characters.name: Orin Vale
characters.description: A polished inventor with old grievances against the missing man and the misfortune of being named by the swan's message.

characters.name: Professor Selda Morcant
characters.description: Precise, severe, and more offended by impossible machinery than by personal insult.

characters.name: Pip Tallow
characters.description: A nervous young mechanic who knows Halcyon House's gears, ducts, and service passages better than any guest.

characters.name: Captain Rusk Fen
characters.description: A square-shouldered officer hired to keep order at the gala, carrying a notebook full of clean conclusions and carefully omitted inconveniences.

items.name: Swan's Prophecy Strip
items.description: A narrow ribbon of cream paper scratched by the automaton's silver beak.
items.inspectText: The message reads, 'ORIN VALE SILENCES THE HAND THAT WOUND THE SWAN.' Beneath the fresh letters are faint pressure marks from an earlier alignment test, as if the strip was fed into a prepared writing action rather than composed spontaneously.

items.name: Fuse Alcove Lever
items.description: A brass-handled lighting lever hidden behind a velvet curtain near the security alcove.
items.inspectText: The lever is warm from recent handling and dust has been rubbed from only one side. It could have cut the gallery lamps without touching the main house controls.

items.name: Patron's Guest Ledger
items.description: Lady Quince's gilt-edged ledger of invitees, investments, and seating arrangements.
items.inspectText: Several investors are marked with anxious sums beside their names. Lady Quince stood to lose heavily if the demonstration failed, though the ledger places her at the front receiving line until the blackout.

items.name: Scored Workroom Latch
items.description: The inner latch of the locked workroom door, marked near the staple.
items.inspectText: Fine scratches run downward from the latch, and a bent sliver of blackened wire lies in the jamb. The bolt could be dropped from outside by someone patient enough to thread the wire through the gap.

items.name: Empty Message-Cylinder Tray
items.description: A velvet-lined tray labeled for the swan's interchangeable instruction cylinders.
items.inspectText: One slot is empty and its dust outline is clean. The missing cylinder would control the beak's writing pattern; swapping it would change the message without rebuilding the automaton.

items.name: Apprentice's Oil Rag
items.description: A rag smelling of violet machine oil, tucked under the workbench.
items.inspectText: The rag bears Pip's stitched initials and oil fresh enough to suggest recent work. A drying smear, however, matches the eight o'clock maintenance oil rather than the nine o'clock disturbance.

items.name: Muddy Uniform Bootprint
items.description: A wet print preserved in canal silt beside the private hatch.
items.inspectText: The sole pattern is standard canal-security issue, but the mud contains bright brass dust of the kind shaken from a watchmaker's file tray. The print points from the service hatch toward the landing, not the street.

items.name: Knotted Mooring Rope
items.description: A short rope left around a dock cleat in a neat, uncommon knot.
items.inspectText: The knot is a double lock-bight used by Bellweather canal officers to secure silent patrol launches. Its tar is still tacky from recent rain exposure.

items.name: Invoice for a Blank Cylinder
items.description: A folded arcade receipt for precision engraving on an unmarked swan cylinder.
items.inspectText: The order is signed 'R. Fen' and dated three days before the gala. It requests a blank cylinder cut to Halcyon House specifications and paid for in canal-security scrip.

items.name: Swan Base Music Box
items.description: A small locked compartment beneath the automaton's pedestal, opened after identifying the removable cylinder system.
items.inspectText: Inside the music-box drum is a thin ledger page in the inventor's hand. It records stolen escapement jewels moved by canal patrol and names Captain Rusk Fen as the officer taking a percentage.

clues.title: The Swan Accuses Orin
clues.content: The public message names Orin Vale, but the pressure marks suggest a prearranged writing action rather than a genuine prophecy or spontaneous accusation.

clues.title: Blackout from the Security Alcove
clues.content: The lamps were cut from a concealed lever near the hired security post, not by a general power failure elsewhere in the house.

clues.title: Lady Quince's Financial Peril
clues.content: Lady Quince had a strong reason to dread a failed demonstration, making her appear suspicious, but the ledger also supports her presence in public view during the crucial minute.

clues.title: Locked Room Faked by Wire
clues.content: The workroom was not proof that the inventor vanished alone; the latch could be set from the corridor after someone removed him through another route.

clues.title: Removable Message Cylinder
clues.content: The swan's writing was governed by a removable cylinder, so a forged accusation could be installed before the demonstration by someone with access or a duplicate part.

clues.title: Pip's Oil Rag Is Misleading
clues.content: Pip handled the swan earlier, but the oil timing points to scheduled maintenance rather than the blackout interval.

clues.title: The Message Could Not Be Composed Live
clues.content: Professor Morcant confirms that the swan cannot reason, improvise, or identify a culprit; it can only execute mechanical instructions prepared in advance.

clues.title: Rusk Claims the Canal Gate Stayed Locked
clues.content: Captain Fen states that no one used the private canal gate during the blackout and that he personally checked it afterward.

clues.title: Security Bootprint at the Hatch
clues.content: A canal-security bootprint links the service hatch to recent dock use, contradicting the claim that the gate remained untouched.

clues.title: Officer's Lock-Knot on the Rope
clues.content: The rope was tied with a canal officer's silent-launch knot, indicating an official boat or officer's hand was involved in the inventor's removal.

clues.title: R. Fen Ordered a Blank Cylinder
clues.content: A blank swan cylinder was ordered in Captain Fen's name before the gala, providing the means to install the false accusation against Orin.

clues.title: The Inventor's Ledger Names Fen
clues.content: The hidden ledger gives Fen a motive: the inventor had documented a canal-security smuggling scheme and intended to expose it once his investors were assembled.

dialogues.question: What did you stand to gain from tonight's demonstration?
dialogues.answer: Gain? Survival, more like. If the swan charmed the investors, Halcyon House would breathe again. If it failed, I would be ruined in silk instead of sackcloth.

dialogues.question: The swan named you. Why would the inventor fear you?
dialogues.answer: Because he enjoyed humiliating rivals in public. I disliked the man, certainly, but murder by parlor toy is not my style. I never touched the swan tonight.

dialogues.question: Could the swan have chosen that accusation by itself?
dialogues.answer: Absolutely not. A mechanism may astonish fools, but it does not acquire conscience in a thunderclap. If it wrote those words, those words were arranged for it beforehand.

dialogues.question: Where were you when the lamps failed?
dialogues.answer: Sent off for violet oil from the workroom shelf, sir. Master said I was hovering. When I came back, everyone was shouting and the swan had already written.

dialogues.question: What did your security sweep find?
dialogues.answer: Nothing useful. The canal gate stayed locked, the crowd stayed inside, and the blackout was over before a thief could cross the gallery. I logged it plainly.

dialogues.question: Your oil rag was found in the workroom. Did you return there during the blackout?
dialogues.answer: No. That rag is mine, but I used it before the guests arrived. Master sent me away just before nine, and I saw Captain Fen near the service corridor as I left.

dialogues.question: What does the empty cylinder tray tell you?
dialogues.answer: That the swan's 'voice' was portable. A practiced hand could replace a message cylinder in less than two minutes, especially while everyone stared at darkness.

dialogues.question: Who had permission to move through the service side of the house?
dialogues.answer: The servants, Pip, my late-arriving caterer, and Captain Fen's men. The captain requested the route himself, claiming it let him guard the canal gate discreetly.

dialogues.question: How do you explain a canal-security bootprint by the hatch?
dialogues.answer: My officers checked the landing before the gala. A print proves diligence, not guilt. As I said, no boat took anyone from my gate tonight.

dialogues.question: Do you recognize this knot?
dialogues.answer: That's not a house knot. Canal officers use it so a launch can be freed without a splash. Master always said it was clever and dishonest-looking.

dialogues.question: This invoice is for a swan cylinder. Is it yours?
dialogues.answer: No. My name is Orin Vale, not R. Fen, and I pay in guild notes, not canal-security scrip. Someone wanted my disgrace to be the loudest fact in the room.

dialogues.question: Would this blank cylinder be enough to forge the swan's message?
dialogues.answer: More than enough. Cut the pins to spell Orin's name, set the starter cam, and the swan becomes a silver-tongued liar on schedule.

dialogues.question: Did the inventor ever mention exposing a crime tonight?
dialogues.answer: Only in hints. He said the swan would bring more than investment to light and warned me not to let Captain Fen handle the machine's base. I thought it was artistic temperament.

dialogues.question: The rope, bootprint, and invoice all point to you. What was in your official report?
dialogues.answer: My report contained what would prevent panic. Yes, I ordered a cylinder as a security test. Yes, I checked the dock. None of that proves I harmed the inventor.

dialogues.question: Why hide a ledger inside the swan?
dialogues.answer: Master trusted gears more than people. He said if anything happened, the swan would keep his true message safe where a thief would not think to read beneath the music.

finalLogic.motive: Captain Rusk Fen was running stolen precision jewels through canal-security patrols. The inventor discovered the scheme, hid a ledger inside the swan's base, and planned to expose Fen before wealthy witnesses after the demonstration secured public attention.
finalLogic.method: Fen used his security access to reach the fuse alcove, cut the gallery lamps, swap in a prepared message cylinder accusing Orin Vale, and remove the inventor through the service hatch to a waiting canal launch. He then reset the workroom latch from outside with wire, reported the canal gate unused, and relied on the forged prophecy to send suspicion toward Orin while the inventor was held at a patrol boathouse.
finalLogic.winEnding: SirLocked and his companion reconstruct the blackout minute, open the swan's base, and confront Fen with the cylinder invoice, officer's knot, dock trace, and hidden ledger. Fen's composure fails when his own security report contradicts the physical trail. The inventor is recovered from the patrol boathouse before dawn, Orin is cleared, and the Clockwork Swan earns fame not as a prophet, but as the machine that preserved its maker's warning.
finalLogic.failEnding: Without the full chain of mechanism, dock evidence, and motive, the accusation against Orin remains persuasive enough to divide the guests. Fen files a polished report, the inventor is moved before the patrol boathouse can be searched, and the swan's false prophecy becomes Bellweather gossip rather than proof.
